packs.desc: 中考核心词，覆盖初中教材高频词

packs.desc: 为达到万词规模补充的通用高频词，非考纲标注

units.title: 学术动词
units.desc: 阅读与写作中最常考的动作类动词，重点在“程度”与“方向”的细微差别。

units.title: 社会议题名词
units.desc: 讨论公共政策、社会现象时的核心名词。

units.title: 评价形容词
units.desc: 表达态度与判断的形容词，注意搭配与感情色彩。

units.title: 熟词僻义
units.desc: 看似基础、实则有第二义项的高频“陷阱词”。

units.title: 论证连接词
units.desc: 议论文与学术写作中的逻辑衔接词。

units.title: 经济与科技
units.desc: 经济、科技类文章的高频名词与术语。

core.en: to make something less severe or harmful
core.ex: Planting trees can mitigate the effects of urban heat.
core.exCn: 植树可以缓解城市热岛效应。
core.note: **辨析** alleviate 多指痛苦、症状的减轻；mitigate 强调降低严重性或破坏力。**词根** mitis（温和）+ agere（做）。

core.en: to provide evidence that proves something
core.ex: The report failed to substantiate its claims with data.
core.exCn: 这份报告未能用数据证实其主张。
core.note: **辨析** verify 侧重核实真伪；substantiate 强调以证据支撑某项主张。**词根** substance（实质）。

core.en: to weaken something gradually
core.ex: Repeated delays undermined public trust in the project.
core.exCn: 一再拖延逐渐侵蚀了公众对该项目的信任。
core.note: **词根** under（在下）+ mine（挖掘）→ 从下面挖空。**搭配** undermine confidence / authority。

core.en: to publicly support an idea; a person who supports it
core.ex: She advocates a gradual reform of the tax system.
core.exCn: 她主张对税制进行渐进式改革。
core.note: **一词多义** 作名词指“拥护者”，作文常用 an advocate of / for。**注意** 动词重音在首音节。

core.en: to limit the range of what can be done
core.ex: Limited funding constrains what the team can achieve.
core.exCn: 有限的经费限制了团队能取得的成果。
core.note: **派生** constraint n. 限制；constrained adj. 受约束的、勉强的。

core.en: to involve something as a necessary part or consequence
core.ex: Any reform entails risks that must be managed.
core.exCn: 任何改革都必然伴随需要加以管控的风险。
core.note: **辨析** involve 中性“包含”；entail 强调“必然带来（代价或后果）”。

core.en: to balance the effect of something
core.ex: Higher efficiency may offset the initial cost.
core.exCn: 更高的效率或许能抵消初期成本。
core.note: **搭配** offset the loss / impact。**词形** offset–offset–offset，过去式与过去分词同形。

core.en: to increase rapidly in number
core.ex: Online courses have proliferated over the past decade.
core.exCn: 过去十年里在线课程数量激增。
core.note: **词根** proles（后代）+ ferre（带来）→ 不断繁衍。**派生** proliferation n.。

core.en: to make two opposing ideas or people agree
core.ex: It is hard to reconcile economic growth with environmental protection.
core.exCn: 很难把经济增长与环境保护协调起来。
core.note: **搭配** reconcile A with B；be reconciled to 甘心接受（不情愿的事）。

core.en: to prove that a statement is wrong
core.ex: The findings refute the assumption that prices always rise.
core.exCn: 这些发现驳倒了“价格总是上涨”的假设。
core.note: **辨析** deny 只是否认；refute 是用证据驳倒。**易混** refuse 拒绝。

core.en: to state clearly as a condition of an agreement
core.ex: The contract stipulates that payment be made within 30 days.
core.exCn: 合同规定须在三十天内付款。
core.note: **辨析** prescribe 规定做法；stipulate 多用于合同、条款。**派生** stipulation n.。

core.en: to produce; to give way; an amount produced
core.ex: The experiment yielded unexpected results.
core.exCn: 实验产生了意想不到的结果。
core.note: **一词多义** yield to pressure 屈服于压力；crop yield 农作物产量。

core.en: to control or limit something harmful
core.ex: The city curbed private car use during the summit.
core.exCn: 峰会期间该市限制了私家车使用。
core.note: **辨析** curb 控制增长势头；restrict 限制范围；ban 明令禁止。

core.en: to cause something to happen
core.ex: Stress can induce sleep problems.
core.exCn: 压力可能引发睡眠问题。
core.note: **辨析** induce 是因果上的“引起”；tempt 是“诱惑某人做某事”。**派生** inducement n.。

core.en: to wear away gradually
core.ex: Inflation erodes household savings.
core.exCn: 通货膨胀逐渐侵蚀家庭储蓄。
core.note: **词根** e-（出）+ rodere（咬）→ 一点点咬掉。**派生** erosion n.。

core.en: something that encourages action
core.ex: Tax breaks offer an incentive to invest.
core.exCn: 税收减免为投资提供了激励。
core.note: **搭配** provide / create an incentive for sb to do。**辨析** motive 指内在动机。

core.en: a difference between things that should be the same
core.ex: There is a discrepancy between the two reports.
core.exCn: 两份报告之间存在出入。
core.note: **辨析** discrepancy 指本应一致却不一致；difference 是中性差异。

core.en: general agreement among a group
core.ex: The committee reached a consensus on the budget.
core.exCn: 委员会就预算达成了共识。
core.note: **搭配** reach / build a consensus。**注意** 通常作单数，不说 a consensus of opinions 之外的复数形式。

core.en: a typical model or framework of thought
core.ex: The discovery shifted the paradigm of modern physics.
core.exCn: 这一发现改变了现代物理学的范式。
core.note: **搭配** paradigm shift 范式转变。**注意** 结尾 -gm 中 g 不发音。

core.en: the level at which something starts to happen
core.ex: Income above this threshold is taxed at a higher rate.
core.exCn: 超过这一门槛的收入按更高税率征税。
core.note: **搭配** cross / exceed the threshold。

core.en: a system in which people or things are ranked
core.ex: Decisions still flow down the corporate hierarchy.
core.exCn: 决策仍沿着公司层级向下传达。
core.note: **派生** hierarchical adj. 分层的。

core.en: the right to make your own decisions
core.ex: Teachers were given greater autonomy over the curriculum.
core.exCn: 教师在课程设置上获得了更大的自主权。
core.note: **辨析** autonomy 强调自主决策；independence 强调不依附。**派生** autonomous adj.。

core.en: a system of official rules that is often slow
core.ex: Small firms complain about the bureaucracy involved in exporting.
core.exCn: 小企业抱怨出口环节的繁文缛节。
core.note: **派生** bureaucratic adj. 官僚的。

core.en: a large and unfair difference
core.ex: The disparity in income between regions has widened.
core.exCn: 地区之间的收入差距进一步拉大。
core.note: **搭配** disparity between / in。**辨析** 强调不公平的差距，比 difference 语气重。

core.en: an earlier case used as an example
core.ex: The ruling set a precedent for similar cases.
core.exCn: 该判决为类似案件确立了先例。
core.note: **搭配** set / create a precedent；without precedent 史无前例。

core.en: the reasons behind a decision
core.ex: The rationale for the change was never explained.
core.exCn: 此次变动的依据从未得到说明。
core.note: **辨析** reason 指一般理由；rationale 指成体系的理据。**注意** 与 rational（理性的）区分。

core.en: a full range of related things
core.ex: Views on the issue cover a wide spectrum.
core.exCn: 对这一问题存在广泛的不同看法。
core.note: **搭配** across the spectrum 在各个层面。

core.en: strong social disapproval attached to something
core.ex: The campaign aims to remove the stigma attached to mental illness.
core.exCn: 这项活动旨在消除精神疾病附带的污名。
core.note: **搭配** the stigma attached to。**派生** stigmatize v.。

core.en: a standard or usual pattern of behaviour
core.ex: Remote work has become the norm in many industries.
core.exCn: 远程办公在许多行业已成为常态。
core.note: **搭配** become the norm；social norms 社会规范。

core.en: an amount that is more than needed
core.ex: The country runs a large trade surplus.
core.exCn: 该国存在巨额贸易顺差。
core.note: **反义** deficit 赤字。**搭配** trade surplus。

core.en: having more than one possible meaning
core.ex: The wording of the clause is ambiguous.
core.exCn: 该条款的措辞含义不明确。
core.note: **辨析** ambiguous 可作两种解释；vague 只是不清楚。**派生** ambiguity n.。

core.en: seeming reasonable or probable
core.ex: She offered a plausible explanation for the delay.
core.exCn: 她为延误给出了一个说得通的解释。
core.note: **辨析** plausible 未必为真但说得通；credible 侧重可信。

core.en: not obvious; delicate and hard to notice
core.ex: There are subtle differences between the two designs.
core.exCn: 两种设计之间存在细微差别。
core.note: **读音** b 不发音，读 /ˈsʌtl/。**派生** subtlety n.。

core.en: strong and unlikely to fail
core.ex: The economy proved surprisingly robust.
core.exCn: 经济表现出乎意料地稳健。
core.note: **搭配** robust growth / evidence / system。

core.en: existing or accepted at a particular time
core.ex: The prevailing view is that regulation is necessary.
core.exCn: 主流观点认为监管是必要的。
core.note: **词根** prevail 盛行。**搭配** prevailing wind 盛行风。

core.en: existing as a natural part of something
core.ex: Every method has inherent limitations.
core.exCn: 每种方法都有其固有的局限。
core.note: **搭配** inherent in。**辨析** intrinsic 侧重本质属性。

core.en: unfavourable or harmful
core.ex: Adverse weather delayed the launch.
core.exCn: 恶劣天气推迟了发射。
core.note: **搭配** adverse effect / impact。**易混** averse 意为“反对的、不乐意的”。

core.en: able to work successfully
core.ex: Solar power is now a viable alternative.
core.exCn: 太阳能如今是一种可行的替代方案。
core.note: **辨析** feasible 偏技术可行；viable 强调现实中能成立、能持续。

core.en: no longer needed; no longer employed
core.ex: Cut redundant sentences to tighten the essay.
core.exCn: 删去多余的句子让文章更紧凑。
core.note: **搭配** be made redundant 被裁员。**派生** redundancy n.。

core.en: easily affected or harmed by something
core.ex: Young trees are susceptible to drought.
core.exCn: 幼树容易受到干旱影响。
core.note: **搭配** susceptible to。

core.en: not able to change or bend
core.ex: Rigid rules discourage innovation.
core.exCn: 僵化的规定会抑制创新。
core.note: **辨析** rigid 不容变通；strict 严格但可合理。

core.en: lasting only a short time
core.ex: The relief was transient.
core.exCn: 这种缓解是短暂的。
core.note: **辨析** transient 强调短暂停留；temporary 指临时安排。**反义** permanent。

core.en: not easily convinced
core.ex: Economists remain skeptical about the forecast.
core.exCn: 经济学家仍对该预测持怀疑态度。
core.note: **搭配** be skeptical of / about。**拼写** 英式 sceptical。

core.en: suggested without being stated directly
core.ex: There is an implicit assumption that growth will continue.
core.exCn: 其中隐含着一个假设：增长将会持续。
core.note: **反义** explicit 明确的。

core.en: stated clearly and in detail
core.ex: The instructions are explicit about deadlines.
core.exCn: 说明中对截止时间有明确规定。
core.note: **搭配** be explicit about。

core.en: to deal with a problem
core.ex: The chapter addresses the question of inequality.
core.exCn: 这一章讨论不平等问题。
core.note: **熟词僻义** 除“地址”外，常考“处理、探讨”，如 address an issue。

core.en: to provide space for; to take into account
core.ex: The hall can accommodate 500 people.
core.exCn: 这个大厅可容纳五百人。
core.note: **熟词僻义** accommodate differing views 兼顾不同意见。**派生** accommodation n.。

core.en: to understand the value or full meaning of something
core.ex: Few appreciate how fragile the system is.
core.exCn: 很少有人意识到这个体系有多脆弱。
core.note: **熟词僻义** 表“意识到”时多接 that / how 从句，是阅读题的高频考点。

core.en: to stop a process from continuing
core.ex: New measures arrested the decline in sales.
core.exCn: 新措施遏制了销量的下滑。
core.note: **熟词僻义** arrest the decline 遏制下滑，属正式书面用法。

core.en: to suppose; to take on responsibility
core.ex: The new manager assumed full responsibility.
core.exCn: 新任经理承担了全部责任。
core.note: **搭配** assume responsibility / control；assuming that 假设。

core.en: to say that something is caused by
core.ex: Researchers attribute the rise to better diagnosis.
core.exCn: 研究者把这一上升归因于诊断水平提高。
core.note: **搭配** attribute A to B。**读音** 作名词时重音在首音节 /ˈætrɪbjuːt/。

core.en: to take advantage of an opportunity
core.ex: Firms capitalized on the demand for remote tools.
core.exCn: 企业利用了对远程工具的需求。
core.note: **搭配** capitalize on 利用（机会），写作中可替换 make use of。

core.en: to provide what a group needs or wants
core.ex: The course caters to beginners.
core.exCn: 这门课程面向初学者。
core.note: **搭配** cater to / for。**辨析** cater to 偶含“迎合不良需求”的贬义。

core.en: to support and defend a cause
core.ex: She championed the cause of rural schools.
core.exCn: 她为乡村学校的事业奔走呼吁。
core.note: **熟词僻义** 动词义近 advocate，常见于人物类阅读。

core.en: to consider an idea seriously
core.ex: The committee entertained the idea of merging.
core.exCn: 委员会考虑过合并的方案。
core.note: **熟词僻义** entertain a proposal 考虑一项提议。

core.en: to base something on; a reason
core.ex: The argument is grounded in solid evidence.
core.exCn: 这一论证建立在扎实的证据之上。
core.note: **搭配** be grounded in；on the grounds that 以…为理由。

core.en: to organize an event; a large number
core.ex: The city hosted the conference last year.
core.exCn: 该市去年主办了这次会议。
core.note: **熟词僻义** a host of 大量，如 a host of problems。

core.en: to officially announce or give out
core.ex: The bank issued new guidelines.
core.exCn: 银行发布了新的指引。
core.note: **熟词僻义** issue a statement 发表声明；the issue of 关于…的问题。

core.en: to make things equal
core.ex: The tax is meant to level the playing field.
core.exCn: 这项税收意在营造公平的竞争环境。
core.note: **搭配** level the playing field 拉平竞争条件。

core.en: to obey a rule; to remark
core.ex: All staff must observe the safety rules.
core.exCn: 全体员工都必须遵守安全规定。
core.note: **熟词僻义** observe the law 遵守法律；observe that 评论说。

core.en: in addition to what has been said
core.ex: The plan is costly; moreover, it may fail.
core.exCn: 该计划成本高昂，而且可能失败。
core.note: **用法** 句首加逗号，正式议论文中用于递进。

core.en: despite what has just been said
core.ex: The evidence is thin; nevertheless, the theory is popular.
core.exCn: 证据薄弱，然而这一理论仍很流行。
core.note: **辨析** nevertheless 表让步转折；therefore 表因果。

core.en: used to compare two different facts
core.ex: Some prefer city life, whereas others seek quiet.
core.exCn: 一些人偏爱城市生活，另一些人则追求宁静。
core.note: **用法** 引导对比从句，前后结构宜对称。

core.en: by that means; as a result of that
core.ex: The firm cut costs, thereby raising margins.
core.exCn: 公司削减了成本，从而提高了利润率。
core.note: **用法** 后接 -ing 表结果，正式书面语。

core.en: in spite of
core.ex: Notwithstanding the risks, the project went ahead.
core.exCn: 尽管有风险，项目还是推进了。
core.note: **用法** 可置于句首或句末，语气正式。

core.cn: 尽管（后接形容词或短语）
core.en: although
core.ex: The recovery is real, albeit slow.
core.exCn: 复苏是真实的，尽管缓慢。
core.note: **用法** albeit + 形容词 / 短语，不接完整从句。

core.en: for this reason
core.ex: Demand fell; hence the price cut.
core.exCn: 需求下降，因此有了降价。
core.note: **辨析** hence 较正式，常与 thus 互换。

core.en: from the opposite point of view
core.ex: Higher prices may boost supply; conversely, lower prices may cut it.
core.exCn: 价格上涨可能增加供给；相反，价格下跌可能减少供给。
core.note: **用法** 引出反向论证，常与 on the contrary 区分：前者表并列对照，后者表否定前说。

core.en: used to say what you think is likely
core.ex: Presumably, the data were collected last year.
core.exCn: 据推测，这些数据是去年收集的。
core.note: **辨析** presumably 基于合理推断；probably 表示概率更高。

core.en: used to give an opinion that may be challenged
core.ex: This is arguably the most important reform in decades.
core.exCn: 这可以说是几十年来最重要的改革。
core.note: **用法** 表达有保留的强主张，学术写作高频。

core.en: according to what some people claim
core.ex: The company allegedly hid the losses.
core.exCn: 据称该公司隐瞒了亏损。
core.note: **用法** 报道未经证实的指控时使用，避免直接断言。

core.en: seeming to be one thing but perhaps not
core.ex: Ostensibly a safety measure, the rule limits competition.
core.exCn: 这项规定表面上是安全措施，实则限制竞争。
core.note: **辨析** 常暗示实际另有目的，与 apparently 语气不同。

core.en: by accident, without intending to
core.ex: The policy inadvertently punished small firms.
core.exCn: 这项政策无意中惩罚了小企业。
core.note: **词根** in-（不）+ advert（注意）。**反义** deliberately 故意地。

core.en: almost not
core.ex: Scarcely had the market opened when prices fell.
core.exCn: 市场刚一开盘价格就下跌了。
core.note: **用法** 句首时主句部分倒装；scarcely…when… 表示“一…就…”。

core.en: in a way that cannot be avoided
core.ex: Trade-offs inevitably involve costs.
core.exCn: 权衡取舍不可避免地涉及成本。
core.note: **派生** inevitable adj. 不可避免的。

core.en: to give money or time for a purpose
core.ex: The budget allocates more funds to research.
core.exCn: 预算向研究拨出更多资金。
core.note: **搭配** allocate A to B。**派生** allocation n.。

core.en: a total formed by combining amounts
core.ex: Aggregate demand fell for a third quarter.
core.exCn: 总需求连续第三个季度下降。
core.note: **辨析** aggregate 指加总后的总量；total 泛指全部。

core.en: a raw material that can be traded
core.ex: Oil remains the most traded commodity.
core.exCn: 石油仍是交易量最大的大宗商品。
core.note: **辨析** commodity 指可交易的原料或标准品；goods 泛指货物。

core.en: the amount by which spending exceeds income
core.ex: The government is struggling with a budget deficit.
core.exCn: 政府正艰难应对预算赤字。
core.note: **反义** surplus 盈余。**搭配** trade / budget deficit。

core.en: a share of profits; a benefit
core.ex: Better training pays dividends in the long run.
core.exCn: 更好的培训从长远看会带来回报。
core.note: **搭配** pay dividends 产生回报。

core.en: a person who starts a business
core.ex: Entrepreneurs often fail before they succeed.
core.exCn: 创业者往往在成功之前屡遭失败。
core.note: **派生** entrepreneurial adj.。**读音** 重音在末音节。

core.en: to change frequently in level
core.ex: Prices fluctuated sharply during the crisis.
core.exCn: 危机期间价格剧烈波动。
core.note: **辨析** fluctuate 指上下起伏；vary 泛指发生变化。**派生** fluctuation n.。

core.en: control of a market by one company
core.ex: The firm was accused of abusing its monopoly.
core.exCn: 该公司被指滥用其垄断地位。
core.note: **派生** monopolize v. 垄断。

core.en: money paid by a government to support something
core.ex: Farmers rely on government subsidies.
core.exCn: 农民依赖政府补贴。
core.note: **辨析** subsidy 指政府补贴；allowance 指津贴、零用钱。

core.en: a tax on goods entering a country
core.ex: New tariffs raised the cost of imports.
core.exCn: 新关税提高了进口成本。
core.note: **辨析** tariff 多指进口关税；tax 为税的总称。

core.en: a set of rules a computer follows
core.ex: The algorithm ranks results by relevance.
core.exCn: 该算法按相关度排列结果。
core.note: **搭配** algorithm-driven 算法驱动的。

core.en: based on observation or experiment
core.ex: The claim lacks empirical support.
core.exCn: 这一主张缺乏实证支持。
core.note: **搭配** empirical evidence / study；与 theoretical 相对。

core.en: basic systems such as roads and power
core.ex: Poor infrastructure holds back growth.
core.exCn: 落后的基础设施制约了增长。
core.note: **搭配** digital / transport infrastructure。

core.en: a statement or situation that seems self-contradictory
core.ex: It is a paradox that scarcity can raise waste.
core.exCn: 稀缺反而可能增加浪费，这是个悖论。
core.note: **派生** paradoxical adj. 自相矛盾的。

core.en: to combine ideas or substances into a whole
core.ex: The review synthesizes findings from 40 studies.
core.exCn: 该综述综合了四十项研究的发现。
core.note: **派生** synthesis n. 综合。
